summaries:
The chapter opens with the narrator, Montresor, vowing revenge against Fortunato for an unspecified insult, resolving to punish him with impunity. On the eve of the carnival season at dusk, Montresor encounters Fortunato, who is drunkenly dressed in motley and prides himself on his wine expertise. Montresor lures him into the family catacombs under the pretense of tasting a pipe of rare Amontillado, exploiting Fortunato’s vanity and intoxication. As they descend into the damp, bone-strewn vaults, Montresor feigns concern for Fortunato’s cough, offering wine to keep him going while subtly guiding him deeper. Upon reaching a hidden niche lined with human remains, Montresor chains Fortunato to the wall under the guise of securing the Amontillado, then begins to brick up the entrance. Fortunato initially laughs, thinking it a joke, but as the wall rises, his cries turn to desperate pleas. Montresor finishes the masonry, silencing him, and leaves him entombed alive. The chapter ends with Montresor’s cold reflection that no one has disturbed the bones for fifty years.
[Characters: Montresor, Fortunato, Luchresi, Lady Fortunato]
